page.title: Renegades
page.t: Inspecting the wreckage, you recover a damaged data recorder and extract a fragment from its message queue:
Inspecting the wreckage, you locate a communications pod containing a partial message in its buffer:
Post-capture inspection reveals a data recorder corrupted during an emergency data purge. A fragment remains accessible within its message queue:
Post-capture inspection reveals a communications pod with signs of an interrupted purge, leaving a partial message preserved in its buffer:
The renegade vessel has been secured and identified. Its systems show signs of disruption, but a data recorder remains functional enough to yield fragments of recorded transmissions.

The shattered hull belongs to a renegade vessel, now identified and destroyed. Among the wreckage, a battered data recorder remains intact, its surface scarred by combat. Whatever this ship was involved in, its trail ends here.

Through careful analysis, reconstruction, and judicious use of a case of confiscated Albion Ale, you decode a fragment indicating that something significant has been staged in [green]%s[/green].

Somewhere in this system lies a faint, deteriorated shipwreck being used as an "entropic gateway segmentation challenger," whatever that means. The wreck and your data scanner appear to be linked to a process referred to as "Renegade Gate Reintegration." The shipboard A.I. cannot make sense of it.

[white]Further analysis suggests the system performs an active verification process. Incorrect inputs appear to trigger defensive countermeasures. %s[/white]
Hey %s, I forgot to give you part %s of the home system code. It`s %s. Memorize it and erase it from your buffers.

%s: Your authorization has been granted for system entry. Please use entry code %s. This information is need to know only and should be stored only in an approved Terracorp encrypted memory module. Do not fail us.
This is Dispatch. The entry code has been set per data security guidelines and is now %s. Please memorize and purge this information from your computer log and communications buffer. Have a nice day.
What`s up, %s? Yea, I was just back at that renegade base for repairs and a bath. The docking bay seemed pretty busy. I saw at least %s class %s ships sitting there, so they seem ready for anything.
Hey, %s, how are things?\n\nI was hunting over in %s and noticed a strange ship hanging out. Thought he may be one of those renegades so I gave him a wide berth. Watch your six, buddy.
No one likes the renegades. We offer them bribes to keep them off our backs.
You did not get this from me, but rumor has it that an %s named %s hired the renegades to attack the Independents. No one knows why the renegades were hired.
You did not get this from me, but rumor has it that a %s named %s hired the renegades to attack the Independents. No one knows why the renegades were hired.
I heard rumors that a fellow pirate named %s is secretly funding the renegades. Do not snitch him out or our heads are next.

[green]The Renegade threat has finally ended![/green]

As you sift through the wreckage, you recover a number of valuable wares still drifting intact in space.

Among the debris, a faint glint catches your eye. Embedded within a ruined data core are engineering specifications detailing improvements to Outpost shipyard design. Your engineers are astounded and immediately begin implementing the changes.

[green]Renegades Plot Reward: Outpost ship specialization increased by 10%[/green].

A few straggler renegades may still be out there somewhere, but they no longer pose a serious threat. Job well done!

[yellow]The Renegades hidden jump gate has been revealed.[/yellow]\n\nYou will have to deal decisively with what lies beyond. Unfortunately for you, the Renegade leaders will now have to deal with you decisively! Expect trouble at your front door. Deal with them before they deal with you.

[green]You have mastered terraforming![/green]

One of your terraforming teams reports back to you. They have found a strange object on one of your planets.

They describe what they`ve found, and you identify the object as an old piece of Terran technology used long ago for terraforming projects. Your scientists run a few benchmark tests, and they confirm that the object is far more advanced than any terraforming equipment you`ve used, advanced enough to improve your terraforming efforts. You give them approval to reverse engineer the object and incorporate its features into your terraformer drones.

[green]Industrial Mastery: Improved planetary engineering and logistics systems allow your empire to support 1 additional terraforming project and 1 additional Mobile Factory per %s planets in your empire.[/green]

Analysis of the recycled Kha'ak vessel has revealed traces of an ancient signal originating from [green]%s[/green]. The vessel's organic structure contains patterns that appear to have been imprinted during its formation within a Kha'ak hive.\n\nYour scientists have traced the signal to an ancient hive buried beneath a planet in the sector. Studying the hive may reveal how the Kha'ak create their organic vessels. The hive appears dormant, but disturbing it may have consequences.

Terraforming operations have disturbed the Ancient Kha'ak Hive. Long-dormant Kha'ak within the planet are awakening and emerging from the Hive.\n\nDefeat the Kha'ak forces before our researchers can safely access the Hive.

The Outpost in [green]%s[/green] has been destroyed. With the containment infrastructure gone, the awakened Kha'ak have consumed what remained of the Ancient Hive. Its secrets can no longer be recovered.\n\nEchoes of the Hive has failed.

The last of the Kha'ak forces emerging from the Ancient Hive have been destroyed. With the Hive secured, your engineers have deciphered enough of its organic structures to reproduce Kha'ak ship designs using conventional shipbuilding techniques.\n\nKha'ak ships can now be constructed in [green]%s[/green].
